title: Generalised Prisms and Euclidean Ramsey Theory
summary: A finite subset $X$ of $\mathbb R^d$ is called Ramsey if for every $k$ there exists an $n$ such that whenever $\mathbb R^n$ is $k$-coloured there exists a monochromatic congruent copy of $X$. K\v rí\v z showed that if there is a soluble group of symmetries of $X$ that acts transitively on $X$, then $X$ is Ramsey. Determining which sets are Ramsey is a major unsolved problem.
